ROLE: Report the lifecycle state so the execution layer can decide which readiness events permit reads or writes and when a session may be reaped.

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: source of the lifecycle state field

VAR.NAME: SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT
VAR.ROLE: returned while no accepted CONNECT has been processed

VAR.NAME: SESSION_READY
VAR.ROLE: returned once CONNACK has been queued

VAR.NAME: SESSION_CLOSING
VAR.ROLE: returned while queued output must still flush

VAR.NAME: SESSION_CLOSED
VAR.ROLE: terminal state, also returned for a NULL session

LOGIC.INPUT: s: borrowed session pointer, possibly NULL.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If s is NULL return SESSION_CLOSED (the terminal value), because a NULL session has no usable descriptor and must be treated as reapable/inactive by callers rather than as a fresh connection. 2) Return s->state verbatim.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: One of SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT, SESSION_READY, SESSION_CLOSING or SESSION_CLOSED. SESSION_CLOSED for a NULL session.
INVARIANTS_USED: SESSION_CLOSED is terminal and implies the descriptor is already closed
state transitions only move forward along the documented state machine
reading state must not change the state machine
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: s is NULL or points to a live session.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Not thread safe with respect to concurrent state transitions on s.
